_doc: Point-in-time retrospective. Every input was public on as_of; see sources. Hindsight lives only in outcome.json.
methodology: house v2 (EPP-distance adjustment), 6-section format; retro method r2: scenario inputs derived from dated facts by frozen rules (retro/README.md); revenue, net-to-gross, expense, receivables and operating-margin signals with Visa's rule-T thresholds

pit_profile.why: 'Visa operates the world’s largest retail electronic payments network and manages a leading global payments brand.' 'We depend heavily upon the overall level of consumer, business and government spending.' 'Within the general purpose payment card industry, we face substantial and intense competition worldwide in the provision of payments services to financial institution customers and their cardholder merchants.' 'Interchange reimbursement fees and related practices have been the topic of recent committee hearings in the U.S. House of Representatives and the U.S. Senate, as well as conferences held by a number of U.S. Federal Reserve Banks.'; no 10-K calls the business cyclical (the economy and spending are a 'why', not the company's own label: the LOW, SHW and JPM reading), so the kind is DURABLE; no disruption theme in taxonomy_eras.json is live for a payments network on these dates, so the watch list is empty

BEAR.desc: Flat EPS (no EPS change in FY09-FY09 to measure: the 0% cap); P/E to its 10th pct

BASE.desc: EPS +13.0%/yr (FY10 revenue guide + margin + buyback); P/E at its 1.8-yr median

BULL.desc: EPS +13.0%/yr (no FY09-FY09 CAGR to measure: BASE's rate); P/E holds its 75th pct

XBULL.desc: EPS +13.0%/yr (no 2-yr run in FY09-FY09: BULL's rate); P/E at its 90th pct

summary: V (retrospective, 2010-08-06) ◉ BUY — Ratio B 0.66x (27.8% downside to Bear $52.08 / +42.2% upside to Bull $102.56) | Adj composite 2.70 vs market 2.56: gap +0.14 [FAIRLY VALUED] | +55% above the EPP floor $46.50 (15x FY10E $3.10) | Conservative 2-yr case: +17.9% total (+9.0%/yr) | At 23.3x FY10E the 15% hurdle price $95.41 sits between the BASE and BULL cases; revenue +23.3% YoY in Q3 FY10, forward revenues +11-15% (FY10 net revenue growth guide); no disruption theme has dated evidence.
